meta_description: Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: There is a plain version of compliance, audit & digital trust: Evidence once, audit anywhere — compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy. We run it with named gates, signed baselines and a weekly evidence cadence — the details are below, in the order they happen.

Compliance dies by spreadsheet: controls tracked in documents, evidence gathered in panic, audits consuming quarters. We implement compliance-as-code — controls expressed once in a framework-agnostic register, tested continuously against your systems, mapped automatically to SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS 4.0, DORA and GDPR/CCPA obligations. Evidence is collected by the platform, not by interns.

For financial-sector clients we extend into operational resilience regimes (DORA: ICT risk, incident reporting, third-party oversight; FCA/PRA operational resilience in the UK), and for anyone handling cards into PCI DSS 4.0 specifics — tokenization architecture, network segmentation evidence, and the new continuous-compliance expectations. The outcome is simple: audits become sampling exercises against a live control plane.

Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust delivery today concentrates in Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Technology & SaaS. The metric is chosen with your finance lead, and the baseline is signed before any build begins.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Framework-unified control register
one control expressed once, mapped to many frameworks
Continuous control testing
automated checks with failing-control workflows
Evidence automation
artifact collection tied to systems, timestamps and owners
DORA & resilience alignment
ICT risk, incident reporting and third-party oversight programs
PCI DSS 4.0 program
tokenization, segmentation evidence and continuous compliance

Weeks nine through thirteen in Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust are the gate: the working slice is measured against the signed baseline, and the scale decision is written down with the evidence attached.
